title: Yol, jol, suol
goal: Place Turkish in its family, and recognize shared words through regular sound correspondences.

intro.text: Turkish has about twenty relatives, from Azerbaijani next door to Sakha in Siberia. Their differences follow rules: Turkish *yol* is `jol` in Kazakh and `suol` in Sakha. Learn a few rules and whole words become recognizable.

vocab.en: branch of a language; (in Turkish usage) a related Turkic language

exercises.question: Which language belongs to the same branch as Turkish?

why.2: Uzbek belongs to the southeastern (Karluk) branch.

exercises.explain: Turkish, Azerbaijani and Turkmen form the Oghuz branch, which is why Turks and Azerbaijanis understand each other well.

exercises.question: Turkish *yol* is `jol` in Kazakh. What is Turkish *yer* (ground, place) likely to be in Kazakh?

why.1: Kazakh changes an initial y, so the Turkish form is unlikely.
why.2: An s for an initial y is Sakha, as in `suol`.
why.3: No rule turns y into k.

exercises.explain: Turkish initial y corresponds to Kazakh j: *yol* and `jol`, *yer* and `jer`.

exercises.question: In Sakha, Turkish *su* (water) is `uu` and *yol* is `suol`. What do the two words show?
options: An initial s disappears, and an initial y becomes s
Sakha adds vowels to every word

why.1: Only the beginnings change, and by rule.
why.2: The point is where y stood: Sakha has s in its place.
why.3: Both are old Turkic words, as the other relatives show.

exercises.explain: Two regular correspondences: Sakha drops an initial s (*su*, `uu`) and has s where Turkish begins with y (*yol*, `suol`).

exercises.title: Almatı'da bir yaz
exercises.passage:
Zeynep bu yaz Almatı'da bir dil kursuna gitti. İlk gün sokakta konuşulan Kazakçayı hiç anlamadığını düşündü. Sonra kulağı alıştı: sayılar tanıdıktı, su yine suydu, yol ise jol olmuştu. Bir dükkânda satıcı ona fiyatı Kazakça söyledi; Zeynep “üş” kelimesini duyunca bunun üç olduğunu hemen anladı.

Kursta öğretmen onlara ilk olarak teşekkür etmeyi öğretti: “Rahmet.” Zeynep bu kelimeyi Türkçeden biliyordu, ama başka bir anlamla. Bir akşam ev sahibi kadın güldü: “Türkçe ile Kazakça kardeş diller, ama kardeşler de birbirini her zaman anlamaz.”

Yazın sonunda Zeynep Kazakça uzun sohbetler edemiyordu, ama alışveriş yapabiliyor, yol sorabiliyordu. En çok da şunu fark etmişti: insanlar onun birkaç Kazakça kelime bilmesine çok seviniyordu.

glossary.en: to chat, to have a conversation

exercises.translation: This summer Zeynep went to a language course in Almaty. On the first day she thought she understood none of the Kazakh spoken in the street. Then her ear got used to it: the numbers were familiar, su was still su, and yol had become jol. In a shop the seller told her the price in Kazakh; when Zeynep heard the word üş, she knew at once that it was üç, three. At the course, the teacher first taught them how to say thank you: 'Rahmet.' Zeynep knew the word from Turkish, but with another meaning. One evening her landlady laughed: 'Turkish and Kazakh are sister languages, but sisters don't always understand each other either.' By the end of the summer Zeynep couldn't hold long conversations in Kazakh, but she could shop and ask the way. Above all, she had noticed one thing: people were very glad that she knew a few words of Kazakh.

questions.q: How did Zeynep understand the price?
options: She recognized üş as Turkish üç
questions.explain: Kazakh has ş where Turkish has ç: *üç*, `üş`.

options: Related languages are close, but not always mutually intelligible

exercises.question: TDK's dictionary gives the example *Çuvaşça ve Yakutça Türk dilinin lehçeleridir.* What does *lehçe* mean here?
options: A branch of the Turkic family that has become a written language

why.1: A local accent is an *ağız*, or in everyday speech a *şive*.
why.2: *Lehçe* names a variety, not an error.
why.3: *Lehçe* is a whole variety of the language, not one word.

exercises.explain: TDK: in some classifications, one of the branches of the Turkish language that have become written languages. Others call them separate Turkic languages, *Türk dilleri*.

exercises.task: In three or four sentences of Turkish, explain how Turkish *yol*, Kazakh `jol`, Kyrgyz `col` and Sakha `suol` are related, and give one more example of the same correspondence.
models: Bu dört kelime aynı kökten gelir ve hepsi yol demektir. Türkçede kelime başındaki y, Kazakçada j, Kırgızcada c, Yakutçada s olur. Bu değişme rastgele değildir; başka kelimelerde de aynı ses denkliği görülür: Türkçe yer, Kazakçada jer olur.

Türkçe yol, Kazakça jol, Kırgızca col ve Yakutça suol akraba kelimelerdir. Aralarındaki fark düzenli bir ses denkliğinden gelir: kelime başındaki y her dilde başka bir sese döner. Aynı kural Türkçe yer kelimesinde de görülür; Kazakçada bu kelime jer diye söylenir.
checklist: The rule stated: *kelime başındaki y … olur*
A second example, such as *yer* and Kazakh `jer`
